Description: The 5NN00 port range (e.g. 50000, 50100, 50200) corresponds to the HTTP interface exposed by the SAP NetWeaver Java stack. These ports are the core access points for J2EE-based SAP services and expose critical enterprise functionality such as administration, user management, and middleware processing. These interfaces are frequently used in Java-only SAP deployments or dual-stack (ABAP + Java) systems.
Deployment Context: These ports are active in NetWeaver Java deployments — particularly in Enterprise Portal (EP), Process Integration/Process Orchestration (PI/PO), and standalone Java Application Server scenarios. They may also appear in dual-stack systems where Java handles specific roles like integration or UI services. The interfaces support various SAP applications, including Web Dynpro, SOAP and REST APIs, and administrative consoles.
Access Behavior: Ports in this range typically expose servlet-based content and are reachable via HTTP (and optionally HTTPS on corresponding 5NN01 ports). While intended for authenticated users within enterprise networks, misconfigurations may leave them externally reachable. These services support session-based authentication and can integrate with SSO technologies such as SAML2 or SPNEGO.
Functional Capabilities: The interfaces often provide access to modules such as SAP Enterprise Portal (/irj/portal), NetWeaver Administrator (/nwa), User Management (/useradmin), Web Dynpro apps, SOAP interfaces (/XISOAPAdapter, /wsnavigator), and REST APIs for PI/PO scenarios. They serve as control points for Java stack operations, and may expose functionality based on assigned roles. JSP-based pages sometimes leak version or patch information.
Security Implications: Historically, SAP NetWeaver Java has been the target of multiple CVEs due to weak authentication handling, verbose error messages, and insecure configurations. Exposed 5NN00 ports may leak version information through login pages, provide unrestricted access to administrative tools, or allow authenticated attackers to elevate privileges. In some cases, misconfigured SSO or forgotten default credentials have led to full compromise.
Detection Goals: This module aims to confirm the presence of NetWeaver Java by probing known endpoints such as /irj/, /nwa/, and /wsnavigator. It will attempt to parse returned HTML or login pages to identify SAP patch levels, enabled modules, and the authentication scheme in use. Further goals include identifying admin vs. user-facing roles and checking for banner leakage.
Assessment Notes: If ports in the 5NN00 range are open and return valid SAP Java content, the host is likely part of a NetWeaver Java deployment — potentially including Enterprise Portal, PI/PO, or administrative subsystems. These ports should be tightly controlled via firewall rules and monitored for abuse. Externally accessible Java ports in particular should be considered high risk without strict access control.
